findings.finding: Pure-play contract foundry: wafer fabrication about 86% of FY2025 revenue; single operating segment; advanced nodes (7nm and below) 79% of Q3 2026 wafer revenue, 3nm 33%, 2nm 8% and ramping. Reports in NT$ under (T)IFRS; the quote is the NYSE ADR, 1 ADS = 5 common shares (25,932m shares = about 5.19bn ADS).

Growth is mostly structural AI/HPC demand plus node mix and price: HPC rose from 58% of FY2025 revenue to 68% in Q3 2026 (+22% q/q), wafer shipments only +9.6% y/y (4.476m vs 4.085m) against revenue +50.9% y/y in NT$, so most of the growth is value per wafer (mix to N3/N2 and price), not volume. FX added: the NT$ growth exceeds the US$ growth (+41.2%). The econ review returned unclassified (no foundry model): the split is this reading, residual not quantified.

Concentrated, US-headquartered demand: North America 75% of FY2025 revenue (customer HQ basis), ten largest customers 78%, Customer A 19% and B 17% (unnamed). No backlog/RPO or take-or-pay disclosed; capital and other purchase obligations NT$1.53tn are TSMC's own commitments, not customer prepayments. Demand ultimately rests on the AI capex of a few hyperscalers and chip designers.

Industry is cyclical by name in the 20-F (owned capacity, high fixed cost, margins fall with utilization) and the history shows one down year (FY2023 revenue -4.5%, operating margin 49.5% to 42.6%). But TSMC's share keeps rising (72.5% of 2Q26 foundry revenue, Samsung 5.9%), growth resumed at +34%/+32%/~+44% in FY2024-26, and the down year was shallow. Treated as structural growth with the cycle carried explicitly in the bear (a 2028 down year).

Computed mature_growth / stalwart confirmed: very large, net-cash, dividend-paying compounder whose growth is currently fast; the type steers the questions (ROIC durability, capex returns, margin at peak), not the numbers.

Conservative guider: revenue beat the guided midpoint in 7 of 7 quarters (Q1 2025-Q3 2026), mean ratio 1.024, above the top of the range in 5. Q4 2026 guide US$52.3-54.3bn (+14% q/q) and FY2026 US$ growth around 44% are therefore floors; the ratio is applied to the Q4 remainder only.

Q2 2026 net income NT$706.6bn includes a NT$63.2bn pre-tax gain on disposal of an equity-method investment (likely the Vanguard stake sale; about 9% of Q2 net income, about US$0.38 per ADR before tax, tax effect not read): normalized Q2 net income is about NT$645-655bn and trailing four-quarter EPS about US$15.2 per ADR rather than US$15.54. Operating income is clean of it. The forecast runs on operating margin, so the gain moves no driver. SBC is negligible (0.03% of revenue) under IFRS. Q3 2026 had no disclosed one-off.

Operating margin 58.7% in Q3 2026 (guide 56.5-58.5% for Q4) against 34.8-50.8% in FY2019-FY2025; management says overseas-fab dilution is about 2 points now and widens to 3-4 points in coming years, plus N2 ramp dilution and tool-price inflation. A run rate at today's margin is a peak-cycle number, not a base.

Piotroski 8/9 strong, Altman Z'' 6.8 safe, ROIC about 53% (avg 53%, incremental 61%) far above the cost of capital; Beneish unavailable. No red flag; the risk is the sustainability of the returns while capex rises to US$60-64bn in 2026 and 'significantly higher' 2026-2028.

Net cash about NT$3.2tn (cash and marketable securities NT$4.02tn vs long-term debt NT$0.82tn at Q3 2026; current debt portion not read). Share count flat (diluted change +0.008% y/y): no dilution, no buyback; returns via a rising quarterly dividend (NT$7.00 for Q2 2026). Capex is funded from operating cash flow (FY2025 FCF NT$1.0tn, 26% of revenue).

flags: Margin at a cyclical peak: operating margin 58.7% vs 35-51% in FY2019-25; overseas-fab dilution widening from ~2 to 3-4 points (bear and base carry it).
Customer concentration: ten largest 78% of FY2025 revenue, two largest 36%; HPC 68% of Q3 2026 revenue: AI-capex digestion risk.
Geopolitics: 80% of noncurrent assets in Taiwan; China-HQ customers 9% of revenue under US export rules; Section 232 tariffs.
One-off: Q2 2026 net income includes a NT$63.2bn disposal gain (tax effect not read); trailing EPS overstated by about 2%.
Capex step-up: US$60-64bn in 2026 and significantly higher through 2028, with tool-price inflation: returns on the new capacity unproven.
Beneish M-score unavailable (inputs missing); equity at 2025-12-31 differs NT$64.6bn between 20-F and 6-K presentation (cause not confirmed).
No attributed consensus and no independent second statement provider: forecasts rest on issuer guidance and history only.

economics.reason: Rising share (72.5% of foundry revenue), node leadership (N2 in volume, A14 2028), value per wafer driving growth and a shallow last down year (FY2023 -4.5%) point to structural growth; the industry cycle is real (20-F risk factor) and is carried as an explicit 2028 down year in the bear rather than normalizing today's revenue.

gaps: No attributed analyst consensus for FY2027 (AV exhausted, FMP denied): FY2027 growth is own-history and guidance-run-rate based.
Econ review unclassified (no foundry model in the registry): growth split not quantified to a residual.
Tax effect of the Q2 2026 disposal gain not read; Q3 2026 consolidated 6-K (operating income, CFO, capex, current debt) not filed until mid-November.
No backlog/RPO, wafer ASP, capacity or CoWoS revenue disclosed; Taiwan production share of revenue not disclosed.
Earlier FY2026 guidance revisions (dates and sizes) not read: only the October 2026 guide is in evidence.
